newsitem.title: USA: Texas mother denies killing sons.
newsitem.headline: Texas mother denies killing sons.

text.p: A mother accused of murdering her two sons took the witness stand at her trial on Wednesday and described herself as a loving parent who could never kill her children.

Darlie Routier, 27, told of the horror of the night of June 6 when she said she awakened to find sons Devon, 6, and Damon, 5, bleeding to death from stab wounds in their Rowlett, Texas home near Dallas.
"I saw Devon laying on the floor. He had cuts and they were so big. I screamed 'Devon, Devon.' I couldn't believe what I was seeing," she said tearfully.
Routier said the boys were killed by an intruder who also gave her superficial stab wounds while she slept nearby.

But prosecutors charge that Routier killed them with a butcher knife in a fit of rage and depression about her weight problems and the family's financial difficulties. They said she inflicted minor stab wounds on herself to cover the crime.
"I loved those children more than my life. No, I did not stab those children, nor did I stab myself," she told the jury just before the defence rested its case.

Routier said she was awakened by Damon tugging at her shoulder and looked up to see the intruder running from the house. She said she never got a good look at the man except to see that he had a dark shirt and cap and had longish hair.
Routier also said she and her housekeeper had seen a car near their house the day before the killings and that the housekeeper told her the driver was peering into their garage.

Prosecutors attempted to point out inconsistencies in Routier's story, including that she testified she had been asleep during the attack, but earlier claimed to have struggled with the intruder. She said her memory of events was clouded.

Routier said she, husband Darin and their sons had enjoyed a normal life before June 6. She downplayed the importance of a May 3 entry in her diary in which she talked about suicide, and also denied that financial problems were bothering her.

"I was feeling, I guess you could say, moody. I'd been having a few days that were really rough," she said. Prosecutor Greg Davis said Routier was taking diet pills at the time of the murders, but she said their only side effect was thirst.
Prosecutors unveiled letters Routier wrote from jail saying she knew who had killed the boys. Routier said she told police of her suspicions, but they had not investigated them.

Prosecutors also questioned her about a graveside birthday party held for Devon on June 14 when he would have been seven. They said Routier showed little regret at the celebration, but she said the party, complete with balloons, music and toys, "was my way to tell Devon 'Happy Birthday.'"
The trial was expected to wrap up this week. Routier faces the death penalty if convicted.
The trial was moved to Kerrville, about 60 miles (95 km) northwest of San Antonio, Texas, because of heavy pre-trial publicity in Dallas.
